Write the run of the real data as one file for a server

Source: R/one_file.R
to_one_file.Rd

to_one_file() writes one R script that runs the scenario "real" of the project on a server without a network. A person pastes the file into R there and runs it from the top to the end.

Usage

to_one_file(...)

Arguments

...

Nothing. A call with an argument stops, and the error names the arguments one_file_home and one_file_folders of initialize_project().

Value

Invisibly, the path of the file. It prints the path, the number of lines, the size in bytes and the length of the longest line.

Details

Call initialize_project() first, in the project on this computer, with the paths of the server as one_file_home and one_file_folders. to_one_file() takes the version, the project and the paths from that call. Without the paths, it stops and prints the two arguments to add. It stops when the run script or a file of the functions folder changed after that call. It needs no results. So you MAY generate and read the file before the first full run. The results on the server go to <one_file_home>/<version>_results/.

The file holds these parts, in this order:

  1. A header with the version of pbn, the date, the project folder and the version. It also gives the md5 of each file in it and the workers.

  2. setwd(home), so that the run script runs in its project folder, as Rscript <version>_run.R does.

  3. The run script as it is written, with three changes. Its call of pbn::initialize_project() gets the paths of the server as home and folders, and the argument generated. generated holds the code of each .R file of the functions folder, in the order that org sources them. The call has no one_file_home, one_file_folders or fake_real_data. The call pbn::scenarios(CFG) becomes pbn::scenarios(CFG, only = "real"). A line with only a comment such as # pbn::to_one_file() is not in the file. The section The md5 of the run script of initialize_project() gives the rule.

  4. A comment that says what to type next, for example pbn::show_blocks().

The section One file of initialize_project() gives the rules of generated. On the server, the run needs no pbn.yml and no functions folder. pbn writes the results and the run log under one_file_home, and, for a data function with cache = TRUE, the cache there too. The manifest holds the md5 of the files of this computer. On this computer, check_one_file() checks that the file gives the real results of the project.

The functions expect_<scenario>() of the fake scenarios of CFG$scenarios are not in the file, because the run has the real data only. The comment lines directly above such a function go with it, up to a blank line or a line with code. expect_real() stays. The fake data code stays, because it is inside the data functions.

The run script MAY give fake_real_data = TRUE for this computer. The file never does, because the server holds the real data.

The file is ASCII, because it goes through a clipboard, which can change a byte that is not ASCII. pbn reads each file of the project as UTF-8 and changes each character that is not ASCII on the parse data, token by token. The files of the project stay as they are:

  • In a string, the character becomes its escape, \uXXXX, or \UXXXXXXXX beyond the BMP, for example "\u2265" for the sign greater than or equal. Every other character of the string stays as it is written, also its quotes, its escapes and its line breaks. In a raw string r"(...)", \u is text and not an escape. So pbn writes such a raw string again from its value. It becomes a normal string in double quotes on one line, with \n for each line break. R does not allow \u in a string with an escape \x or an octal escape. So pbn writes such a string from its value too. The code of the file is identical() to the code of the project. Such a string gets the encoding mark "UTF-8" where the string of the project MAY have "unknown", and identical() treats the two as equal.

  • In a comment, the character becomes the text <U+XXXX>.

  • In a name, for example a name in backticks, to_one_file() stops, because R reads a name only as it is written.

to_one_file() stops when, and writes no file:

  • the run script has not exactly one top-level call pbn::initialize_project(), or not exactly one call pbn::scenarios(CFG) with no other argument. It names what it found.

  • a file in the file holds a name that is not ASCII, a NUL, or a line that is not UTF-8. It also stops on a string that is not valid UTF-8 after its escapes. The error names the file and the line.

  • a path of the server or the name of the project folder is not ASCII.

  • code that stays in the file uses a name of an expect_<scenario>() that the file leaves out. The file would stop on the server. The error names the file and the line.

  • the assignment of such a function shares a line with other code. That is text before it on its first line, or text other than a comment after it on its last line.

  • the file does not parse.

The file has LF line ends. pbn does not cut long lines, and it prints the length of the longest line. The file keeps the workers of pbn::run_plan() of the run script, and its header says how to change it. The paths go into the file as they are given, so give / in a path for Windows too, for example "N:/durable/project".

The file is always <version>_one_file.R in the folder of the project of the last initialize_project() of this R session. The printed line names that folder.

These are limits of the file:

  • The comments of the code go into the file as they are written, with <U+XXXX> for a character that is not ASCII. So a comment with a path of this computer reaches the server.

  • The rule no_absolute_paths of check_project() does not see a path with one name such as "/data", or a path that paste0() or sprintf() builds. Such a path in the code reaches the server too.

Put the file in git. It is what ran on the server. check_project() knows its name, and its code rules do not read it, because it holds the paths of the server by design.

See also

vignette("pbn"), section "Running on an air-gapped server".
